turnaround_reason: Gogo fell ~78% from its $16.82 high to ~$3.65 (near 52-week lows) as legacy air-to-ground revenue stagnated and Starlink invaded business-aviation connectivity. The turnaround bet is the Galileo HDX LEO antenna (Eutelsat OneWeb) plus the completed Satcom Direct acquisition, which together make Gogo a multi-orbit/multi-band provider targeting the ~64% of business jets still lacking broadband, especially international and military/government.
bullish_points: Hard product catalyst underway: 150+ Galileo HDX antennas shipped and multiple FAA STCs secured (G650, PC-12), giving direct LEO competition to Starlink
Satcom Direct acquisition adds international + MilGov exposure and higher-margin service/government revenue
Very cheap on forward earnings (~4.5x forward PE) with positive FCF (~$24M) and 15% operating margins
Meaningful insider conviction: Director Townsend bought 250k shares (~$1.1M) at $4.54-4.57 in March 2026; insiders hold ~25%
Large untapped TAM — only ~36% of global business jets are broadband-equipped
Analyst targets $7-12 (mean $9.5) imply large upside from $3.65, albeit thin coverage (2 analysts)
bearish_points: Heavy leverage: ~$903M debt vs ~$107M cash (debt/equity ~765), EV ~$1.3B — little margin for execution error
Revenue still declining (-1.7% YoY) and thin net margins (~1.5%); trailing PE ~36
Starlink is a formidable, well-capitalized competitor already entrenched in business aviation since 2023
Satcom Direct integration risk plus a leadership transition announced at deal close
Analyst price target already cut to $7 from $11 — sentiment deteriorating even among bulls
Options are effectively illiquid (double-digit OI), no leveraged expression
catalyst: Q2 2026 earnings — the market wants Galileo HDX shipment/backlog acceleration and Satcom Direct accretion to service revenue and margins
suggested_trade: Small spot position only; starter around $3.50-3.80 near 52-week-low base, size for the high leverage/binary execution risk
key_risk: Starlink continues taking share while the debt load forces defensive capital allocation, stalling the Galileo/SD ramp before it inflects revenue
would_skip_if: Q2 shows Galileo HDX shipments plateauing or service revenue not inflecting; or you cannot tolerate a highly levered small-cap with a declining top line
